title: Monomorphisms into disjoint unions of field spectra
statement: Let $I$ be a set and $(k_i)_{i\in I}$ a family of fields [def-weil-field]. Put $D=\coprod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Spec}k_i$, the disjoint union scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For every monomorphism of schemes $m:T\to D$ there is a subset $J\subseteq I$ and an isomorphism $T\cong\coprod_{j\in J}\operatorname{Spec}k_j$ over $D$, with $m$ the corresponding component inclusion. Here monomorphism means that for every scheme $H$ the function $\operatorname{Hom}(H,T)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H,D)$ is injective. Both the empty family and an infinite family are allowed.

proof.text: Write $\iota_i:\operatorname{Spec}k_i\to D$. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] their images $D_i$ are disjoint clopen subsets covering $D$. Set $T_i=m^{-1}(D_i)$, with open inclusion $j_i:T_i\to T$; these opens are disjoint and cover $T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme], $m j_i=\iota_i f_i$ for a morphism $f_i:T_i\to\operatorname{Spec}k_i$. It is monic: if $f_i a=f_i b$, then $m j_i a=m j_i b$, hence $j_i a=j_i b$ by monicity of $m$, and $a=b$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism].

Monicity of $f_i$ gives injectivity on morphisms from every field spectrum. The equivalence (1) with (2) in [def-weil-radicial-morphism] therefore makes $f_i$ universally injective, hence injective on points by the identity base change. A field spectrum has one point by [def-weil-affine-spectrum], so $T_i$ has at most one point. If $T_i$ is nonempty, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] gives an affine open containing its point; its underlying open is all of $T_i$, so $T_i\cong\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ is affine.

For a nonempty $T_i$, write $f_i=\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_i)$ with $\varphi_i:k_i\to A_i$, using the affine identification and [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. This ring map is epic: if $a,b:A_i\to B$ satisfy $a\varphi_i=b\varphi_i$, functoriality gives $f_i\operatorname{Spec}a=f_i\operatorname{Spec}b$; monicity of $f_i$ and uniqueness of the ring map inducing an affine morphism give $a=b$. Apply [lem-sfb-field-ring-epimorphism-trivial-or-iso]. The zero-ring case would make $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ empty, since a prime ideal is proper and a zero ring has no proper ideal. Thus $\varphi_i$ is an isomorphism and functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ makes $f_i$ an isomorphism.

Let $J=\{i\in I:T_i\ne\varnothing\}$. The $T_j$ for $j\in J$ still form a clopen decomposition of $T$, so [det-pe-finite-local-systems-type-coproduct] says their inclusions present $T$ as their coproduct. Put $C=\coprod_{j\in J}\operatorname{Spec}k_j$ with inclusions $\eta_j$, using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. The two universal properties define $\theta:C\to T$ by $\theta\eta_j=j_j f_j^{-1}$ and $\psi:T\to C$ by $\psi j_j=\eta_j f_j$. Both composites restrict to the identity on each coprojection, so $\theta$ and $\psi$ are inverse. Moreover $m\theta\eta_j=\iota_j$, proving the assertion over $D$. This includes empty $J$ and empty $I$, and uses no finiteness of the index set.
